'''Thomas Quinn Jones''' (born August 19, 1978) is an American actor and former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played as a [[running back]] for 12 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Jones played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia Cavaliers]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 1999. He was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] seventh overall in the [[2000 NFL draft]], and played for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in addition to the [[New York Jets]], [[Chicago Bears]], and [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. He retired among the top 25 leading rushers in NFL history (currently 27th<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/rush_yds_career.htm | title=NFL Rushing Yards Career Leaders| website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>), and a member of the [[List of National Football League career rushing yards leaders|10,000 rushing yards club]]. In September 2019 he was nominated for the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] Class of 2020.<ref name="nfl.com">{{Cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001053757/article/reggie-wayne-troy-polamalu-lead-firsttime-hof-candidates | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915132138/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001053757/article/reggie-wayne-troy-polamalu-lead-firsttime-hof-candidates | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 15, 2019 | title= Reggie Wayne, Troy Polamalu lead first-time HOF candidates | website= [[NFL.com]] | date = September 12, 2019 | access-date = September 14, 2019}}</ref>

In 2013, performing under the name Thomas Q. Jones due to the [[SAG-AFTRA]]'s [[Stage name#Union rules|unique stage name requirements]], he began an acting career.<ref>{{Cite web|last=writernymagee|date=October 14, 2020|title=Thomas Q. Jones says 'acting became therapy' after NFL career|url=https://thegrio.com/2020/10/14/thomas-q-jones-says-acting-became-therapy/|access-date=August 20, 2021|website=TheGrio|language=en-US}}</ref> Among his credits are 2015's ''[[Straight Outta Compton (film)|Straight Outta Compton]]'' and a recurring role in the [[Luke Cage (TV series)|''Luke Cage'']] series.

'''Thomas A. Lewis''' (born January 10, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[New York Giants]]. He was selected by the Giants in the first round of the [[1994 NFL draft]] out of [[Indiana University]] with the 24th pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1994 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1994/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> While at Indiana, he set a [[Big Ten]] record and tied an NCAA record with a 99-yard touchdown reception against [[Penn State]] on November 6, 1993.  That same day, he set a Big Ten record with 285 receiving yards. Thomas Lewis was the Varsity head coach at Chaparral High School in Scottsdale, Arizona for 2 years before resigning on January 12, 2018. He was the last Hoosier to be drafted in the first round until the Las Vegas Raiders drafted Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the first overall pick 32 years later.

([[Gatesville, North Carolina]]) | college = [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] | draftyear = 1993 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 28 | pastteams = * [[Buffalo Bills]] ({{NFL Year|1993|1999}}) * [[Chicago Bears]] ({{NFL Year|2000}}) * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|2001}}) | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Tackle]]s | statvalue1 = 347 | statlabel2 = [[Interception]]s | statvalue2 = 6 | statlabel3 = Forced [[fumble]]s | statvalue3 = 3 | pfr = SmitTh21 }} '''Thomas Lee Smith''' (born December 5, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) who played for the [[Buffalo Bills]], [[Chicago Bears]], and [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]]. After being selected 28th overall in the first round of the [[1993 NFL draft]], Smith played primarily on special teams during the 1993 season.{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He played in [[Super Bowl XXVIII]] for the Bills against the Dallas Cowboys.{{Cite web |title=Thomas Smith Playoffs Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitTh21/gamelog/post/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He became a starting cornerback for Buffalo in 1994, a position he would hold through the 1999 season. During this time, Smith became known as one of the top coverage cornerbacks in the NFL, but did not receive the Pro Bowl and/or All-Pro recognition his play deserved because of a lack of interceptions (at the time, advanced coverage statistics which would have benefited superb lockdown players like Smith did not exist, and his lack of interceptions was wrongly cited when he was seen as a good rather than great player). He left Buffalo following 1999 to sign with the Chicago Bears, where he played in 2000. He finished his playing career with the Indianapolis Colts in 2001.
